findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource internal id instead of name
findings.body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the lambda iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` and uses `groupResource.getId()` (the resource's own internal primary key) both as the argument to `hasPermission(...)` and as the value added to the granted set. The resource is created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` -> `resolveGroup`, which sets the resource's NAME to `group.getId()`; the resource's internal id is a separate generated value. Downstream, `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e. it tries to look up a resource by NAME using the resource's own internal id. That lookup always misses, so the code falls through to the `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (all-groups) placeholder resource and runs the scope evaluation there. The consequence: (a) when the admin has any policy on the all-groups placeholder, the placeholder's internal id is added to the granted set and then placed in `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` so the user search filters against a non-existent group id, potentially excluding users even when per-user `canViewByGroup` would grant visibility; (b) for per-group-only setups the function returns an empty set, silently disabling the `UserModel.GROUPS` pre-filter optimization (the `canView` per-user check is the only thing that carries correctness). The fix is to use `groupResource.getName()` for both the `hasPermission` argument and the value added to the granted set, and additionally skip the all-groups placeholder resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE.equals(groupResource.getName())`) so it isn't treated as a real group id.

findings.title: Double semicolon in field initializer
findings.body: `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` has two semicolons after the constructor call. Harmless but worth fixing while the file is being touched.
